subject: Post-call: reserved GPU commitment criteria, isolation & burst policy confirmation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Reddy <arjun@neurolytics.ai>, Elena Soto <elena.s@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: reserved GPU commitment criteria, isolation & burst policy confirmation

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we have alignment. TL;DR: NeuroLytics is prioritizing strict tenant isolation (VPC + workload-level isolation), predictable throughput for inference (target 1.2M tokens/day with 99th-percentile latency targets), and a procurement window in early May.

Key pain points you called out:
- Multi-tenant leakage risk: must guarantee VPC-level isolation and customer-managed KMS.
- Predictable tail latency for user-facing API (p99 target 450ms at 8 token prompt baseline).
- Cost control during training-like bursts — need a defined burst policy and clear overage model.

What we propose (initial):
- Reserved pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2, dedicated to your account (physical isolation within a tenancy group).
- Burst policy: allowed bursting up to 24 GPUs for short windows (configurable rate-limit + billing uplift).
- SLA targets: 99.95% availability for the reserved pool; latency SLOs we can feature at p50/p95/p99 depending on workload shapes; default p99 goal 450ms for <512 token requests.
- Data controls: customer KMS integration + audit logs retention 90 days (we can scope to 30 days if required).

Deliverables I attached: redwood-dedicated-playbook.pdf (ops runbook), isolation-matrix.xlsx (mapping of isolation controls), SOC2-summary.pdf (security baseline).

Next steps / owners:
- Rishi: technical deep-dive / performance modelling session (action: propose bench config and estimates) — target this week.
- Jordan: procurement + commercial terms (action: draft pricing bands for reserved vs burst and contract timeline).
- Arjun / Elena: send procurement checklist and confirm decision window (you mentioned early May).

Can you confirm those priorities and whether the proposed reserved capacity (16 GPUs) + burst to 24 matches your internal calc? If yes, I’ll have Jordan kick off a preliminary commercial proposal and Rishi schedule a 90-minute technical workshop.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Arjun Reddy <arjun@neurolytics.ai>

Date: 2027-04-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: reserved GPU commitment criteria, isolation & burst policy confirmation

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Isolation: VPC-level isolation is a hard requirement. We need tenancy that prevents noisy-neighbor at the network and hypervisor level. Also want a short whitebox review of the isolation model (diagram + attestation).
2) KMS: customer-managed keys are required; keys will live in our AWS account and we need to encrypt inference payloads at rest and in transit with our KMS.
3) Retention: Our legal team pushes for 30 days of request logs and ability to map a dataset to deletion on demand. Is that feasible?
4) Pricing / procurement: We need clear per-GPU reserved pricing + burst uplift. Also please include committed spend bands and cancellation terms.

We attached our procurement requirements to this reply (NL_procurement_requirements.xlsx). Our timeline: procurement expects a signed term sheet by May 7 so we can include in Q2 budget.

If Rishi can run a modelling session early next week that would be great. We can do Tue 10am PT (Apr 20) for the technical workshop.

Best,
Arjun Reddy
CTO, NeuroLytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: reserved GPU commitment criteria, isolation & burst policy confirmation

+Technical notes (quick):
- Topology: We can provision a physically isolated reserved pool in us-west-2 (tenant-dedicated cluster) sized at 16 A100 equiv. Burst to 24 will be implemented via pre-warmed spare nodes and autoscale policy keyed to queue depth; burst windows recommended <= 2 hours to avoid preemption costs.
- Latency modelling: For your avg prompt (8 tokens in, 64 tokens out) and the model family you mentioned, 16 GPUs at continuous ~60% utilization should meet the daily throughput target (1.2M tokens/day) and keep p99 around 350–480ms depending on exact seq lengths and batching. I’ll put numbers into a spreadsheet during the workshop.
- KV cache: plan to use prefix KV caching for inference hot paths to reduce per-token cost and hit p99. Cache warmup choreography will be part of the runbook.
- KMS: We support AWS KMS customer-key integration; engineering will need cross-account IAM role and a short attest/action list for key rotation.

Action items:
- I’ll prepare a short performance estimate (tokens/sec per GPU under expected batch sizes) and a canary plan for a staged rollout.
- We should capture exact retention SLA (30 vs 90 days) — Jordan to confirm commercial impact.

Quoted from Kimberly’s email for context:
> "Reserved pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2, dedicated to your account (physical isolation within a tenancy group)."

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
